reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Verified code at gossip_methods.rs:745-765. The 01e requirement (file: 01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json, invariant: 'Gossip validation IGNORE must not forward but allow later re-processing of the message') is satisfied by protocol-level semantics, not application-level reprocessing queues. The code correctly returns MessageAcceptance::Ignore for FutureSlot/PastFinalizedSlot (doesn't forward, allows peer retry). Phase 03's interpretation conflates 'reprocessable' (protocol allows retry) with 'must have explicit queue'. Comparison with other message types confirms this is intentional: gossip blocks (L1295-1307), blob sidecars (L900-919), and data columns all handle FutureSlot identically—IGNORE without queuing. Only ParentUnknown triggers explicit reprocessing (L691-694, L851-854) because it's a dependency issue, not timing. Attack scenario is not exploitable: clock-skewed messages are retried by honest peers when timing is correct; PeerDAS redundancy and sync mechanisms (by_range/by_root) ensure availability; no single column loss causes network-wide failure. This is by-design clock tolerance, not a bug. Severity: original LOW is overinflated—no exploitable impact, spec-compliant design pattern.
